grades.quote: CAS is typically used by lock-free and wait-free algorithms.
grades.reason: Introduces the RISC-V Zacas compare-and-swap extension, which can be used for lock-free counters. It does not describe an atomic increment or returning the previous value, so it only gives background.

Gives a worked RISC-V example that atomically increments a 64-bit counter with AMOCAS.D. The old memory value is loaded into the rd register pair and checked for retry. It is a CAS-based retry loop and not a single increment-and-return-old-value instruction, and the passage does not state the return semantics explicitly.
Describes LoongArch version evolution. It mentions byte/half-word atomic memory access instructions only in passing and says nothing about atomic increment or returning the previous value.
Covers cycle counting in the Control Transfer Records extension. It has nothing to do with atomic memory increments.
